questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) guidelines?

options.text: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are clearly specified.
Method of blinding is clearly specified.
The randomization procedure is clearly specified.

questions.explanation: The Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) statement, most recently updated in March 2010, is an evidence-based minimum set of recommendations, including a checklist and flow diagram for reporting randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and is intended to facilitate the complete and transparent reporting of trials and aid their critical appraisal and interpretation. In CONSORT guidelines, there is intention-to-treat analysis instead of per-protocol analysis. Another feature is that all patients assessed for the trial are accounted for, and the report is accompanied by a diagram that summarizes the outcomes of all patients involved in the trial.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a proper randomization method used in randomized controlled trials (RCTs)?
questions.explanation: Quasi-randomization is not a proper randomization method, as it is based on subjects’ characteristics, such as date of birth, and confounders can exert effects. Centralization randomization is done by a remote computer and third party to avoid selection bias. In minimization, to ensure the balance of factors between groups, the next allocation depends on the characteristics of subjects already being allocated. For stratified randomization, subjects are subdivided into strata, and individuals within each striatum are then randomized. In stepped-wedge randomization, the population is divided into groups, and then the intervention is progressively introduced, in random order, across the groups until every group is receiving it. This is used when other allocation methods would be unfeasible because of widespread belief that the intervention is beneficial.

questions.question_text: What percentage of patients diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) have HIV-associated neurocognitive impairment?
questions.explanation: Early cognitive impairment occurs in 20% of patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). It can be classified into cognitive, behavioural and motor symptoms. Cognitive symptoms include poor memory, concentration impairment and mental slowing. The patient may need a written reminder to help them to recall. Behavioural symptoms include apathy, reduced spontaneity and social withdrawal. Depression, irritability, agitation and psychotic symptoms may occur. Motor symptoms include loss of balance, poor coordination, clumsiness and leg weakness. In the later stages, there will be global deterioration of cognitive functions, and this is manifested by word-finding difficulties. Patients may exhibit psychomotor retardation and mutism. The prevalence of dementia in patients suffering from acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) is around 25%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following complications best describes a man who recovered from herpes encephalitis and subsequently develops very good appetite, weight gain and high sexual drive?
questions.explanation: Devic syndrome, also known as neuromyelitis optica, is a variant of multiple sclerosis. Churg Strauss syndrome presents with asthma, pulmonary infiltrates and vasculitic phase involving the peripheral and central nervous system (CNS), heart, lungs, kidney and gastrointestinal tract. Hallervorden–Spatz disease is a rare familial disorder with extrapyramidal symptoms, aggression and gradually developing dementia. Tolosa–Hunt syndrome presents with unilateral orbital pain with cranial nerve third, fourth and sixth nerve palsies.

questions.question_text: The court decision is that the murder charge is reduced to manslaughter in view of diminished responsibility as a result of the abnormality of the mind. Which of the following terminologies correctly describes the above?
questions.explanation: The above correctly describes what is commonly referred to as voluntary manslaughter. Involuntary manslaughter refers to an unlawful and dangerous act; the actus reus (committing an act that is known to be against the law) consists of an unlawful act that is dangerous and cause death. Whereas, gross negligence refers to the actus reus, which consists of a breach of a duty of care that the accused owes to the victim, with the result that this breach leads to the victim’s death.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding various types of offenders is correct?

options.text: A hepatologist refers a patient with hepatitis B to you. She is a 55-year-old woman with no previous offences and is an active member of her church. She has just been convicted of shoplifting. In this case, the most likely cause is depression.
In the United Kingdom, homicide of the father is more common than that of the mother.
Castration of violent offenders and reduction of testosterone have shown resultant significant reductions in violent offending.
Cautioning is not a common disposal method for female offenders.
Research studies have suggested that raised levels of serotonin turnover and alterations in dopamine metabolism occur in violent offenders.

correct_answer.text: Research studies have suggested that raised levels of serotonin turnover and alterations in dopamine metabolism occur in violent offenders.

correct_answers.text: Research studies have suggested that raised levels of serotonin turnover and alterations in dopamine metabolism occur in violent offenders.

questions.explanation: Only 1% of offenders have depressive disorder, and the most common cause is not related to psychiatric disorder. Matricide (killing one’s own mother) is more common than patricide (killing one’s own father). Thirty percent of mothers who commit filicide (killing one’s own children) have psychiatric illness. Physical castration has no impact, while chemical castration shows conflicting results. Cautioning is the main disposal used for female offenders (50% in females versus 30% of males). Research studies have suggested that raised levels of serotonin turnover and alterations in dopamine metabolism occur in violent offenders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Lesch–Nyhan syndrome?
questions.explanation: About 85% of those with Lesch–Nyhan syndrome exhibit self-injurious behaviour. The age of onset of self-injurious behaviours is usually before 3 years. Lips and fingers are often bitten. Generalized aggression with temper tantrums directed against objects and people are also seen. Other features include microcephaly, hypotonia followed by spastic choreoathetosis, dysphagia and dysarthria. The incidence of Lesch–Nyhan syndrome is 1 in 10,000 to 1 in 38,000, and it is exclusive to men. It is an X-linked recessive condition involving CAG trinucleotide repeats and is due to a defect in hypoxanthine guanine phosphoribosyl-transferase resulting in accumulation of uric acid.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would you not expect to observe in the electroencephalogram (EEG) reading of an elderly person with normal ageing?

options.text: No significant increase in delta activity
A significant increase in delta and theta frequency
A small decrease in alpha frequency
A small increase in theta activity
A small increase in beta frequency

correct_answer.text: A significant increase in delta and theta frequency

correct_answers.text: A significant increase in delta and theta frequency

questions.explanation: A significant increase in delta and theta frequency, together with a decrease in beta activity and slowing of dominant alpha frequencies, is a characteristic EEG finding associated with dementia. A small decrease in alpha frequency may be seen from age 50 onwards. A small increase in beta frequency is also correlated with age. Normal age is generally associated with a non-significant increase in delta activity.

questions.question_text: The presence of eosinophilic inclusion bodies is most likely to be found in which of the following types of dementia?
questions.explanation: The eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies refer to Lewy bodies that contain accumulated alpha synuclein.

questions.question_text: Which personality disorder (PD) is associated with suicide in the elderly?
questions.explanation: Higher levels of neuroticism, and lower scores for openness to experience and having a restricted range of interests are the personality subtype associated with suicide in the elderly.

questions.question_text: What is the percentage of children with autistic disorder also suffering from mental retardation?
questions.explanation: Previous epidemiological study has shown that 70% of children with autism have mental retardation. Approximately 30% have mild-to-moderate mental retardation, and around 50% have severe-to-profound mental retardation. Other comorbid disorders include academic learning problems in literacy and numeracy, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), tics or Tourette syndrome, anxiety disorders, depression, temper tantrums, oppositional defiant disorder as well as self-injurious behaviour.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding personality changes across adulthood is false?

options.text: Personality retains stable over long periods.
Personality changes greatly over long periods.
There is an increase in the dimension of agreeableness.
There is a decline in the dimensions of extraversion.
There is a decline in the dimensions of openness to experience.

correct_answer.text: Personality changes greatly over long periods.

correct_answers.text: Personality changes greatly over long periods.

questions.explanation: Several longitudinal studies have shown stability of personality over long periods of life. Studies have also shown a decrease in the dimensions of neuroticism, extraversion and openness to experience and increases in agreeableness and conscientiousness across a lifetime.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding coping in the elderly is true?

options.text: Involvement in religion and having spiritual beliefs do not help.
The elderly have less emotional reactivity when encountering stress compared with younger adults.
Minority groups use less religious coping when faced with difficulties.
The elderly have the same level of internal control as younger adults.
Retirement increases the risk of psychiatric disorders and leads to poorer coping in the elderly.

correct_answer.text: The elderly have less emotional reactivity when encountering stress compared with younger adults.

correct_answers.text: The elderly have less emotional reactivity when encountering stress compared with younger adults.

questions.explanation: Studies have shown that older people have less emotional reactivity when encountering stress and higher levels of internal control compared with younger adults. Religious involvement and having strong spiritual beliefs have been found to help alleviate the negative effects of some life experiences. Marginalized minority groups have been found to use religious coping more often when encountering problems. Retirement has not been shown to increase the risk of psychiatric disorders and poor coping skills.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old man who has been diagnosed with acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) is on follow-up with you for depression. He is keen to have psychological treatment in addition to medication. Which of the following therapies would you recommend?
questions.explanation: The most commonly effective type of psychological intervention in people with HIV/AIDS is cognitive behavioural stress management.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychiatric disorders is least commonly seen in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome?
questions.explanation: The prevalence of chronic fatigue syndrome in the United Kingdom ranges from 0.8% to 2.6%. The female-to-male ratio is 3:1. The age of onset is between 29 and 35 years old. People with chronic fatigue syndrome may have lower occupational status and educational background. Aetiologies of chronic fatigue syndrome include persistent viral infection, immune dysfunction, electrolyte imbalance and chronic candidiasis. Immunological changes involved include increased expression of activation markers on T lymphocytes, increased CD-8+ cell numbers and decreased natural killer cell function. Endocrinological changes include HPA axis abnormalities and hypocortisolism. It is most commonly associated with depression and anxiety. Individuals with chronic fatigue syndrome are at greater risk than those without for current psychiatric disorder. Patients with chronic fatigue syndrome are more likely to have received psychotropic medication or experienced psychiatric disorder in the past. There is a trend for previous psychiatric disorder to be associated with comorbid rather than non-comorbid chronic fatigue.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a defence mechanism associated with obsessions?
questions.explanation: In reaction formation, there is a psychological attitude that is diametrically opposed to an oppressed wish and constitutes a reaction against it. This is often seen in patients with OCD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following randomization methods is the least likely to produce bias in a randomized controlled trial?

options.text: Allocation of patients by their month of birth
Allocation of patients by hospitalization status (inpatient versus outpatient)
Allocation of patients by gender (stratified randomization)
Allocation of patients by laboratory results
Allocation of patients by order of arrival time in clinic

correct_answer.text: Allocation of patients by gender (stratified randomization)

correct_answers.text: Allocation of patients by gender (stratified randomization)

questions.explanation: This is stratified randomization, while the other options are quasi-randomization. For stratified randomization, subjects are subdivided into strata, and individuals within each striatum are then randomized. This is less likely to produce bias in RCT compared with quasi-randomization, which is not a proper randomization method, as it is based on subjects’ characteristics, such as month of birth, hospitalization status and laboratory results.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not increase the power of a randomized controlled trial?

options.text: Comparison of active treatment with placebo
An increase in the number of collaborating centres instead of the number of subjects
Using observer-rated questionnaires instead of self-reported questionnaires

correct_answer.text: An increase in the number of collaborating centres instead of the number of subjects

correct_answers.text: An increase in the number of collaborating centres instead of the number of subjects

questions.explanation: The power of a RCT depends on sample size, total number of endpoints, difference in compliance between two groups, increased number of endpoints by selecting a high-risk population or increased duration of follow-up. Having more collaborating centres does not necessarily mean more subjects, which is important in increasing the power of an RCT.

questions.question_text: In the brief intervention for alcohol dependency with the acronym FRAMES, what does the ‘E’ stand for?
questions.explanation: FRAMES stands for feedback about drinking, responsibility enforcement, advice to change, menu of alternatives, empathetic style and self-efficacy.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old man was brought in by his parents, as he insists on waiting for a man to take revenge on him at the bus station. He appears to be odd in his speech and behaviour. Which of the following supports the diagnosis of schizotypal disorder?

options.text: Abnormal ideas but consistent with cultural norms.
The onset of symptoms occurs at the age of 14 years.

correct_answer.text: The onset of symptoms occurs at the age of 14 years.

correct_answers.text: The onset of symptoms occurs at the age of 14 years.

questions.explanation: Schizotypal disorder runs a chronic course (at least 2 years). People with schizotypal disorder may have odd beliefs inconsistent with cultural norms, obsessive ruminations without inner resistance, transient quasi-psychotic episodes but not as intensified as first-rank symptoms and poor rapport.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding vitamin B12 deficiency is false?

options.text: It may present with macrocytic anaemia and neuropathy.
Psychosis may occur with the deficiency.
Measurement of vitamin B12 should be done in an elderly man presenting with cognitive impairment.
Serum homocysteine level is not a good indicator of vitamin B12 or folate status.

correct_answer.text: Serum homocysteine level is not a good indicator of vitamin B12 or folate status.

correct_answers.text: Serum homocysteine level is not a good indicator of vitamin B12 or folate status.

questions.explanation: Serum homocysteine level may serve as a functional indicator of vitamin B12 status, as it is needed to convert homocysteine to methionine in one-carbon metabolism in brain tissue. Deficiencies in vitamin B12 and folate can lead to neuropsychiatric disorders, including neuropathy, depression, psychosis and cognitive impairment.

questions.question_text: A 68-year-old man presents to your clinic with worsening memory impairment and difficulty in finding words. You diagnose him to have Alzheimer’s disease. His family has read up on apolipoprotein E (APOE) testing and is keen for him to undergo the test to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment. Which one of the following statements regarding this test is true?

options.text: Homozygous for APOE allele is diagnostic for Alzheimer’s disease.
This test is recommended to be done to predict the risk of dementia in asymptomatic persons.
The results of this test can help guide response to cholinesterase inhibitors.
The presence of the APOE allele is a risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease.
The presence of APOE alleles increases the specificity of the diagnosis of Lewy body disease.

correct_answer.text: The presence of the APOE allele is a risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease.

correct_answers.text: The presence of the APOE allele is a risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease.

questions.explanation: Several studies have shown presence of the APOE allele to be a risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease. It also increases the specificity of the diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease. Homozygous for APOE allele is not diagnostic for Alzheimer’s dementia. APOE testing is not currently recommended for predicting the risk of dementia in asymptomatic persons. Response to cholinesterase inhibitors in patients is also not influenced by results of APOE testing.

questions.question_text: After Alzheimer’s disease, which of the following is the leading cause of dementia in elderly people?
questions.explanation: The second most common cause of dementia is vascular dementia, which accounts for 15%–30% of cases. It includes disorders arising from either large or small vessel strokes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be the most appropriate antidepressant to maintain a pregnant female on?
questions.explanation: Selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors can cause pulmonary hypertension (after 20 weeks) in the newborn. Neonates may experience withdrawal (agitation and irritability), especially with paroxetine and venlafaxine. Amitriptyline and imipramine have been used for many years without causing teratogenic effects. The use of tricyclic antidepressants in the third trimester may lead to withdrawal effects and increase the risk of preterm delivery. Fluoxetine has the most data on safety. Paroxetine is associated with foetal heart defects in the first trimester and is less safe than other SSRIs. Sertraline may also decrease Apgar scores.

questions.question_text: A 70-year-old man has been diagnosed to have early-onset dementia. Which of the following difficulties is the most likely to manifest earliest?

options.text: Rapid forgetting of new information after short intervals

correct_answer.text: Rapid forgetting of new information after short intervals

correct_answers.text: Rapid forgetting of new information after short intervals

questions.explanation: Short-term memory loss is the earliest manifestation of Alzheimer’s disease. Visuospatial problems and semantic knowledge problems become more prominent in the later stages of the illness. Speech comprehension, which is a fundamental element of communication, is better preserved.

questions.question_text: Which of the following hormone levels is not decreased in patients with anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: The following hormones are decreased in patients with anorexia nervosa: FSH, LH, oestrogen and T3. In contrast, CRH, cortisol and growth hormone levels are increased. With the reduction in circulating oestrogen, there is shrunken uterus and small amorphous ovaries. As weight is gained, the uterus increases in size, and the ovaries become multifollicular. At normal weight, the ovaries become follicular: this is detected by the pelvic ultrasound and can be used to indicate correct weight. The electrolyte disturbances include hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, hypozincaemia and hypophosphataemia.

questions.question_text: The cognitive impairments noted in Alzheimer’s disease are most correlated with which one of the following histological abnormalities?
questions.explanation: In Alzheimer’s disease, histological changes include granulovascular degeneration, Hirano bodies, neurofibrillary tangles and senile plaques. The correlation between the density of postmortem neurofibrillary tangles and cognitive impairment is more robust than with other histological abnormalities.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man with no medical or psychiatric history presents with vocal and motor tics that resemble Tourette syndrome. He is noted to have taken some antibiotics a week ago. Which of the following antibiotics could he have taken to cause his presentation?
questions.explanation: The psychiatric side effects of cephalosporins include euphoria, delusions, depersonalization and illusions. The side effects of clarithromycin include delirium and mania, whereas the side effects of gentamicin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole include delirium and psychosis. The side effects of quinolones include psychosis, paranoia, mania, agitation and Tourette-like syndrome. Risk factors of neuropsychiatric side effects from antibiotics have included prior psychopathology, coexisting medical conditions, slow acetylator status, advanced age, concomitant medications and increased permeability of the blood–brain barrier, as well as high antibiotic dosage and intrathecal or intravenous administration. Psychiatric toxicity may result from various mechanisms of action, including antagonism of GABA or pyridoxine, adverse interactions with alcohol, or inhibition of protein synthesis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding the conduction of a randomized controlled trial?

options.text: A multi-centred trial is preferred to assess effects of trial drug in different ethnic groups because of variation in pharmacokinetics.
A patient can withdraw from the randomized controlled trial at any time and a valid reason is required.
Placebo treatment is not recommended in chronic and severe illnesses.
The RCT needs to obtain ethics committee approval beforehand.
The RCT should be guided by the uncertainty principle, and both investigators and subjects should not know the efficacy of trial drug and gold-standard treatment.

correct_answer.text: A patient can withdraw from the randomized controlled trial at any time and a valid reason is required.

correct_answers.text: A patient can withdraw from the randomized controlled trial at any time and a valid reason is required.

questions.explanation: This option is contrary to the Declaration of Helsinki, which states that research subjects can withdraw from study without giving any reason. Steps involved in the conduction of RCT include identify and engage investigational sites, develop trial governance procedures, develop trial procedures according to good clinical practice, apply and obtain funding, develop recruitment strategies and methods to identify and overcome recruitment problems, develop data capture methods, engage in oversight of trial progress, develop procedures for adverse event reporting and complete trial termination procedures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding sample size and power?

options.text: Precision is increased by reducing the size of the standard error.
Power is increased by having a larger clinically relevant difference.
A power of 0.8 means that it gives an 80% chance of detecting a difference.
The size of the standard error is based on the size of the sample.
The larger the sample size, the larger the standard error.

correct_answer.text: The larger the sample size, the larger the standard error.

correct_answers.text: The larger the sample size, the larger the standard error.

questions.explanation: The larger the sample size, the smaller the standard error. Increased statistical power is associated with larger sample size, larger meaningful difference and smaller standard deviation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Hypothalamic harmatoma is associated with epilepsy, precocious puberty and hypothalamic rage.
Patients with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM) have more cognitive impairment than patients with non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (NIDDM).
Diabetes insipidus is associated with generalized anxiety.
Addison’s disease is associated with hypercalcaemia, hyponatraemia and lethargy.

correct_answer.text: Patients with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM) have more cognitive impairment than patients with non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (NIDDM).

correct_answers.text: Patients with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM) have more cognitive impairment than patients with non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (NIDDM).

questions.explanation: Patients with IDDM tend to have less cognitive impairment than patients with NIDDM.

questions.question_text: Patients with AIDS can present with mania that may have a different presentation from that of primary mania. Which of the following is not a typical characteristic of AIDS mania?
questions.explanation: AIDS mania has a clinical picture that is rather different from primary mania. There is irritable mood, which can be prominent, although euphoria may still be observed. There can be psychomotor slowing that accompanies the cognitive slowing of the AIDS dementia, replacing the expected hyperactivity of mania. This form of mania is also more chronic than episodic, with infrequent spontaneous remissions.

questions.question_text: With regard to the pharmacological management of social phobia, which of the following medications has been shown to be particularly helpful?
questions.explanation: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors are effective in agoraphobics and social phobics, with at least 80%–90% of pure social phobia individuals being asymptomatic with 16 weeks of treatment. However, patients who are withdrawn from treatment suffer from relapse. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors such as citalopram, fluvoxamine, paroxetine and sertraline are usually used as first-line treatment. Benzodiazepines can also help to prevent the reinforcement of fear through avoidance. Beta blockers can be particularly useful for performance anxiety.

questions.question_text: The lifetime prevalence of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has been estimated to be around
questions.explanation: Based on the Epidemiologic Catchment Area study, it was found that OCD is very rare in children. Rutter found no cases among the 2,000 10- and 11-year-olds in the Isle of Wight. Other findings were that the 6-month prevalence of OCD has been estimated to be around 1.3%–2.0%; the lifetime prevalence has been estimated to be around 1.9%–3.0%; there is an equal sex ratio, and there is a bimodal peak of onset at 12–14 and 20–22 years of age. There is a decline in onset after age 55.

questions.question_text: The syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) is more likely to be associated with which of the following psychotropic medications?
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine may cause SIADH. The mechanism for this is uncertain but may involve increased release of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) and/or potentiation of the action of this hormone.

questions.question_text: Which of the following PDs has been found to be associated with the highest rate of post-transplant non-compliance?
questions.explanation: Perioperative psychosocial characteristics are strong and significant predictors of noncompliance. Strategies to improve compliance should focus on psychosocial risk factors pertaining to early psychologic reactions to transplantation, the quality of family relationships and patient coping styles. These factors are potentially modifiable through educational and supportive interventions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following concepts regarding the stochastic damage of ageing is false?

options.text: Macromolecules distort the physical and chemical properties of the human body.
There is irreversible cessation of mitosis and ultimately the death of an organism.
The accumulation of earlier adverse events in ageing eventually leads to the end of survival.
There is decline in basic metabolic rate as a person gets older.

correct_answer.text: There is irreversible cessation of mitosis and ultimately the death of an organism.

correct_answers.text: There is irreversible cessation of mitosis and ultimately the death of an organism.

questions.explanation: The essential concept of stochastic damage talks about wear and tear as a result of ageing. Macromolecules distorting the physical and chemical properties of the human body, free-radical damage, accumulation of earlier adverse events and a decline in basic metabolic rate are concepts related to this theory. Irreversible cessation of mitosis and ultimately the death of an organism are related to the Hayflick limit theory, which involves genetically programmed ageing.

questions.question_text: An antidepressant was found to be more likely to reduce the score of the Hamilton Depression Scale by 50% from baseline score compared with placebo (n = 3000 patients, 10 centres, relative risk for remaining depressed = 0.30; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.2–0.6; absolute risk difference = 0.42; 95% CI 0.2–0.6). What is the 95% CI number needed to treat (NNT) with this antidepressant to prevent one additional patient from remaining depressed?
questions.explanation: The number needed to treat (NNT) is the reciprocal of the absolute risk difference. The 95% confidence interval for NNT is obtained by 1 divided by the upper and lower limits of the absolute risk difference. Thus CI is 1/0.6 to 1/0.2, which equals approximately 1.67–5.00.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding psychosis secondary to traumatic brain injury is false?

options.text: Delusions are more common than hallucinations.
Increased severity of brain injury increases the risk of psychosis.
Onset of psychosis is usually gradual and occurs within 6 months after the injury.
Negative symptoms are less common than hallucinations.
Temporal lobe lesion is a risk factor for psychosis.

correct_answer.text: Onset of psychosis is usually gradual and occurs within 6 months after the injury.

correct_answers.text: Onset of psychosis is usually gradual and occurs within 6 months after the injury.

questions.explanation: The onset of psychotic symptoms is usually gradual and delayed, often occurring more than one year after the injury. Risk factors for psychosis include temporal lobe and left-hemisphere lesions, closed head injury and increasing severity of brain injury. Delusions are more common than hallucinations. Negative symptoms are less common than hallucinations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following about anorexia nervosa and hormones involved is incorrect?

options.text: There is a decrease in CRH.
There is an increase in the amounts of cortisol.
There is an increase in growth hormone.
There is a decrease in both FSH and LH.
There is a decrease in oestrogen for females.

correct_answer.text: There is a decrease in CRH.

correct_answers.text: There is a decrease in CRH.

questions.explanation: There are multiple hormonal changes in anorexia nervosa. The typical changes are decreased T3, increased CRH, increased cortisol and increased growth hormone, as well as decreased FSH and LH. The 24-hour pattern of LH secretion resembles that of a pre-pubertal individual. There is a decrease in oestrogen in women.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding exhibitionism is false?

options.text: Exhibitionism is included in both DSM and ICD.
One of the best predictors of recidivism is lack of empathy.
50% of sexual offences seen by courts are related to exhibitionism.
Exhibitionists are more likely to be married than other sexual offenders.
The reconviction rate is low after a first conviction but high after second conviction.

correct_answer.text: 50% of sexual offences seen by courts are related to exhibitionism.

correct_answers.text: 50% of sexual offences seen by courts are related to exhibitionism.

questions.explanation: The true figure is only about 25%. Less than 20% of indecent exposers will re-offend.

questions.question_text: Which of the following findings from the National Confidential Inquiry into Suicide and Homicide (United Kingdom) is incorrect?

options.text: Approximately 25% of people who committed suicide had been in recent contact with mental health services before death.
The period of highest risk of suicide after discharge from inpatient care is the first 14 days.
Over one-fifth of individuals dying by suicide have not been adherent to medication in the preceding month of their death.
In the United Kingdom, around 50 homicides per year are committed by those in recent contact with mental health services.
The rate of ‘stranger homicides’ by those with mental illness has increased sharply.

correct_answer.text: The rate of ‘stranger homicides’ by those with mental illness has increased sharply.

correct_answers.text: The rate of ‘stranger homicides’ by those with mental illness has increased sharply.

questions.explanation: There is no increase in 'stranger homicides' by those with mental illness. In the UK, approximately 35% of homicides are committed by offenders with psychiatric illnesses. Among these, schizophrenia accounts for 55%, personality disorder 26% and affective disorder 19%. Less than half of psychotic offenders describe psychotic motivation. Approximately 160–200 psychiatric inpatients die by suicide annually, most commonly by hanging.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old man suffering from schizophrenia is admitted due to worsening of psychotic symptoms. The urine cannabis screen is negative (level of cannabinoids <20 ng/ml), despite the fact that his partner confirms he is a heavy user of cannabis. The core trainee wants to consult you on the underlying reason. The following are possible reasons except which one?

options.text: The urine screen was done on the fourth day after admission, and the active ingredient of cannabis was not detectable.
The person adulterated his urine sample with vinegar.
The person drank a lot of water and alcohol prior to the urine test.
The person took 10 tablets of aspirin 12 hours before the urine test.
The person took a lot of vitamin B prior to the test and then diluted his urine with water.

correct_answer.text: The urine screen was done on the fourth day after admission, and the active ingredient of cannabis was not detectable.

correct_answers.text: The urine screen was done on the fourth day after admission, and the active ingredient of cannabis was not detectable.

questions.explanation: This explanation usually applies to a first-time or occasional user. In heavy users, THC metabolites can be detectable for up to six weeks because they are stored in body fat. Adulteration with vinegar, excessive fluid intake and aspirin interference with immunoassays, as well as vitamin B cocktails, are all known methods to reduce detectability.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old woman develops her first episode of anorexia nervosa. Her mother is very concerned and gathers some information on the outcome of her illness. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: This patient has good prognosis, as she has a relatively late onset.
The most common switch in pattern is from anorexia nervosa to bulimia nervosa.
The most common switch in pattern is from bulimia nervosa to anorexia nervosa.
The outpatient treatment should be 3 months, duration for those patients without hospitalization.
30% will have a duration of illness longer than 12 years.

correct_answer.text: The most common switch in pattern is from anorexia nervosa to bulimia nervosa.

correct_answers.text: The most common switch in pattern is from anorexia nervosa to bulimia nervosa.

questions.explanation: The course and outcome of anorexia nervosa are variable. Some patients recover fully after a single episode, some exhibit fluctuating weight gain followed by relapse. Among adolescents, around 80% recover in 5 years and 20% develop chronic anorexia nervosa. Among adults, 50% recover, 25% have intermediate outcomes and 25% have poor outcomes. Fifty percent of restrictive-type anorexia nervosa patients develop bulimia nervosa after 5 years. The disorder has substantial mortality (5%–20%), with an aggregate mortality rate of 5.6% per decade, 12 times the annual death rate for all causes in females aged 15–24. The mortality rate is higher than for psychiatric inpatients and the general population.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following deficits is unlikely to be found in a patient with caudate nucleus dysfunction (e.g. Huntington disease)?
questions.explanation: Huntington disease is a genetic disorder with continuous involuntary movements and progressive dementia. Common deficits in caudate nucleus dysfunction include apathy, depression, disinhibition, personality change, aphasia, psychosis and a predisposition for delirium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications has been associated with paradoxical agitation in patients with traumatic brain injury?
questions.explanation: Gabapentin is an anticonvulsant structurally related to GABA. It has been reported to cause paradoxical agitation in some patients with traumatic brain injury. Physicians prescribing gabapentin for neuropathic pain in brain-injured patients should monitor for signs of restlessness or anxiety.

questions.question_text: The NHS wants to decide which antidepressant is to be used to treat depression. Only cheaper antidepressants will be chosen, and outcome is not important. Which type of economic analysis is being used in this scenario?
questions.explanation: Cost minimization analysis is used to find the least expensive method of achieving a single outcome. Its advantage is simplicity, but it assumes equivalent effectiveness of interventions and compares solely on cost. Cost effectiveness analysis compares treatments with differing costs and benefits measured in natural units, cost–utility analysis measures outcomes in quality-adjusted life years, and cost–benefit analysis measures both costs and benefits in monetary terms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true for disulfiram?

options.text: Halitosis is an uncommon side effect.
It is contraindicated in people with advanced liver disease.
It decreases the level of warfarin and theophylline.
It inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase leading to accumulation of acetaldehyde.
The starting dose is 100 mg daily.

correct_answer.text: It is contraindicated in people with advanced liver disease.

correct_answers.text: It is contraindicated in people with advanced liver disease.

questions.explanation: Disulfiram inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, leading to acetaldehyde accumulation after alcohol ingestion and producing unpleasant effects (flushing, tachycardia, hypotension). The usual starting dose is 800 mg followed by 100–200 mg daily. It increases warfarin, theophylline and diazepam levels via drug interactions. It is contraindicated in advanced liver disease, cardiac failure, coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease and in pregnancy and breastfeeding.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false for acamprosate?

options.text: It is a GABA antagonist and glutamate agonist.
It reduces craving in people with chronic alcohol dependency.
Significant benefits will continue 1–2 years after stopping.
It can be combined with disulfiram.

correct_answer.text: Significant benefits will continue 1–2 years after stopping.

correct_answers.text: Significant benefits will continue 1–2 years after stopping.

questions.explanation: Acamprosate is a GABA agonist and glutamate antagonist. It inactivates NMDA receptors and prevents calcium influx, rebalancing GABA and glutamate in abstinence. Its effect is most pronounced at 6 months and remains significant up to 12 months but not 1–2 years after stopping. It can be combined with disulfiram. Contraindications include severe renal or hepatic impairment, pregnancy and breastfeeding.

questions.question_text: A 10-year-old boy with learning disability has fair skin and blue eyes. He also has self-mutilating and stereotyped behaviour. He suffers from epilepsy and has been eating a special diet since he was a baby, as recommended by his paediatrician. Which one of the following statements regarding his condition is false?

options.text: He has to take a high-phenylalanine diet.
The incidence of his condition is 1 in 4,500–15,000.
This disorder involves a defect in the phenylalanine hydroxylase leading to accumulation of phenylalanine.
The screening test for this disorder is the Guthrie test soon after birth.
The mode of inheritance is autosomal recessive.

correct_answer.text: He has to take a high-phenylalanine diet.

correct_answers.text: He has to take a high-phenylalanine diet.

questions.explanation: The boy has phenylketonuria, caused by phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency leading to phenylalanine accumulation. Management requires a low-phenylalanine diet initiated before 6 months of age to preserve intelligence; not a high-phenylalanine diet. Side effects of the diet include anaemia, hypoglycaemia and oedema.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old man who has epilepsy presents with white skin patches and gingival fibromata. Whole-body scan shows tumours in his lungs, spleen and kidneys. Several members of his family, including his father and one of his sisters, are affected. Which one of the following statements regarding his condition is true?

options.text: A Wood’s lamp or ultraviolet light may be used to locate the hypomelanotic macules.
It is autosomal dominant with 70% penetrance.
Males are more affected than females.
The majority of those affected have profoundly low IQ.

correct_answer.text: A Wood’s lamp or ultraviolet light may be used to locate the hypomelanotic macules.

correct_answers.text: A Wood’s lamp or ultraviolet light may be used to locate the hypomelanotic macules.

questions.explanation: Tuberous sclerosis is autosomal dominant with 100% penetrance. Males and females are equally affected. The majority have normal IQ; if there is learning disability, it is usually profound. Seizures are common, often presenting as infantile spasms. Hypomelanotic macules can be highlighted with a Wood’s lamp.

questions.question_text: Major depression is associated with lesion(s) in which part of the brain after a cerebrovascular accident?
questions.explanation: Approximately 30% of stroke survivors develop major depression. Depression is more common in lesions of the left frontal lobe and left basal ganglia, especially in the acute post-stroke period. Right-sided strokes leading to depression often have a family history of mood disorder. Lesion volume correlates with depression severity.

questions.question_text: A 12-year-old child has a happy disposition with paroxysmal laughter. He frequently flaps his hands and has jerking movements. He has a history of severe learning disability and epilepsy. Which one of the following statements about his condition is false?

options.text: Patients with this condition have attention-deficit syndrome and sleep disturbance.
The prevalence of this condition is 1 per 20,000 to 1 per 30,000.
Severe mental retardation is commonly seen.
Severe psychomotor retardation is attributed to abnormal expression of UBE3A.
70% have microdeletions of chromosome 15q11–13 of paternal origin.

correct_answer.text: 70% have microdeletions of chromosome 15q11–13 of paternal origin.

correct_answers.text: 70% have microdeletions of chromosome 15q11–13 of paternal origin.

questions.explanation: This is Angelman syndrome, due to maternal deletion of chromosome 15q11–13 (not paternal). It presents with happy disposition, paroxysmal laughter, hand flapping, severe learning disability, ataxia, epilepsy, attention problems and sleep disturbance. About 70% have the maternal deletion; paternal uniparental disomy accounts for another 2–5%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions is associated with severe mental retardation?
questions.explanation: Cornelia De Lange syndrome is associated with severe-to-profound learning disability. Klinefelter syndrome, Turner syndrome, Wilson disease and XYY syndrome are associated with milder cognitive impairment when present.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a strength of cohort study?

options.text: It is able to follow temporal relationships.
It measures multiple effects of a single exposure.
It is useful for diseases with long latency periods.
It is well suited to rare exposures.

questions.explanation: Cohort studies can establish temporal relationships, measure multiple outcomes of a single exposure, and are useful for diseases with long latency periods and rare exposures. However, they tend to be expensive and time-consuming, and loss to follow-up can bias results.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has the lowest incidence of mental retardation?
questions.explanation: Only about 30% of males with Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) have learning disability, usually mild, whereas Cornelia De Lange, Fragile X, Prader–Willi and Smith–Magenis syndromes are associated with higher rates of intellectual impairment.

questions.question_text: Based on the NICE guidelines, which of the following modalities of psychological therapy has not been recommended for patients with anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: Recommended therapies for anorexia nervosa include cognitive analytical therapy, cognitive-behavioural therapy, interpersonal therapy, focal dynamic therapy and family interventions. Dialectical behavioural therapy is not recommended.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about pharmacotherapy for eating disorders is incorrect?

options.text: Pharmacological treatment should not be used as the sole or principle treatment for anorexia nervosa.
With regard to the usage of antipsychotics for anorexia nervosa, olanzapine has been the most studied antipsychotic.
Oestrogen administration should not be considered for use to help treat bone density problems in children and adolescents, as this might lead to problems in development.
Upon weight restoration, fluoxetine has demonstrated benefits for patients with anorexia nervosa.
Selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are the first-line drugs of choice for the treatment of patients with bulimia nervosa.

correct_answer.text: Upon weight restoration, fluoxetine has demonstrated benefits for patients with anorexia nervosa.

correct_answers.text: Upon weight restoration, fluoxetine has demonstrated benefits for patients with anorexia nervosa.

questions.explanation: Fluoxetine has failed to demonstrate benefits in treating anorexia nervosa after weight restoration. Olanzapine has been associated with weight gain, reduced obsessionality and anxiety. Estrogen should not be used in adolescents for bone density due to risk of epiphyseal fusion. SSRIs are first-line for bulimia nervosa, particularly fluoxetine at 60 mg/day.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true for case–control studies?

options.text: Bias can be adjusted for at the analysis stage.
Confounding factors are defined as any factors that affect outcome.
It is often difficult to find age-matched controls.
In the design of case–control studies, confounding factors must be completely excluded.
Logistic regression can adjust for only one factor at a time.

correct_answer.text: It is often difficult to find age-matched controls.

correct_answers.text: It is often difficult to find age-matched controls.

questions.explanation: Case–control studies match individuals with the outcome (cases) to those without (controls). It is often difficult to find suitably age-matched controls. Bias cannot be fully adjusted for, confounding factors cannot be completely excluded in design, and multivariable logistic regression can adjust for multiple factors simultaneously.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old man is brought in by the police for punching a man in the face and smashing his car window screen in his driveway. His explanation is that the other driver drove too close to his car and stared at him. This is the fourth time he has hit someone for ‘pissing him off’ over the last year. He admits to having difficulty controlling his temper and having a tendency to go into a rage when he gets annoyed. He usually feels guilty after the episodes. He has no psychotic symptoms, and there is no history of alcohol drinking or illicit drug use. Which of the following diagnoses is most likely?
questions.explanation: Intermittent explosive disorder is a behavioural disorder characterized by extreme expressions of anger, often to the point of uncontrollable rage, disproportionate to the provocation. Impulsive aggression is unpremeditated and disproportional. Some individuals report affective changes (tension, energy shifts) before outbursts. Diagnosis requires multiple episodes of assault or property damage out of proportion to the situation and not better accounted for by mania, psychosis, antisocial personality or medical conditions.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old with schizophrenia on risperidone complains of sexual dysfunction. Which of the following tests would you order?
questions.explanation: Risperidone leads to an increase in prolactin level and sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding hyperthyroidism and manifestations of neuropsychiatric symptoms is true?

options.text: The prevalence of cognitive impairment in hyperthyroidism is more than in hypothyroidism.
The majority of patients with hyperthyroidism will exhibit some form of psychopathology.
In hyperthyroid patients with depressive symptoms, mood symptoms may precede physical symptoms.
Hypomania is the most common psychiatric manifestation.

correct_answer.text: In hyperthyroid patients with depressive symptoms, mood symptoms may precede physical symptoms.

correct_answers.text: In hyperthyroid patients with depressive symptoms, mood symptoms may precede physical symptoms.

questions.explanation: Serious psychopathology is present only in a minority of patients; mood symptoms may precede development of physical signs and symptoms of hyperthyroidism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is inherited in an autosomal-dominant fashion?
questions.explanation: DiGeorge syndrome is caused by a microdeletion in chromosome 22q11.2 and is inherited in an autosomal-dominant fashion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a sex-linked recessive disorder?
questions.explanation: Lesch–Nyhan syndrome is an X-linked recessive disorder.

questions.question_text: A 7-year-old boy has developmental delay, hypertrichosis, deafness and joint stiffness, with claw hand and hepatosplenomegaly. Which condition is most likely?
questions.explanation: Sanfilippo syndrome (mucopolysaccharidosis III) presents with developmental delay, hypertrichosis, deafness, joint stiffness, claw hand and hepatosplenomegaly.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is relatively preserved even in the advanced stage of Huntington disease?
questions.explanation: In advanced Huntington disease, language functions are relatively preserved compared to other cognitive domains.

questions.question_text: The Family Environment Scale measures the social climate of families. Which of the following is not an area of this rating scale?
questions.explanation: Bonding is not one of the subscales of the Family Environment Scale.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the Conners Rating Scale–Revised is true?

options.text: It includes parents, teacher and youth self-report versions.
It includes parents and youth self-report versions only.
It does not assess common comorbid conditions.
The behaviour scale does not include assessment of cognitive problems.

correct_answer.text: It includes parents, teacher and youth self-report versions.

correct_answers.text: It includes parents, teacher and youth self-report versions.

questions.explanation: The Conners Rating Scale–Revised includes parent, teacher and youth self-report versions and assesses ADHD symptoms, anxiety, cognitive problems, oppositional behaviour, perfectionism and social problems.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding intelligence tests is true?

options.text: IQ scores are weakly associated with academic achievement.
IQ scores are strong predictors of overall adjustment.
Intelligence test scores are fairly stable for children above the age of 5 years.
IQ scores are strongly associated with socio-emotional functioning.
The Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children measures socio-emotional functioning in children and adolescents.

correct_answer.text: Intelligence test scores are fairly stable for children above the age of 5 years.

correct_answers.text: Intelligence test scores are fairly stable for children above the age of 5 years.

questions.explanation: Intelligence test scores are generally unstable in preschool children but become fairly stable after age 5; IQ scores are strongly associated with academic achievement but only modestly with overall adjustment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a shared commonality between the genders with regard to conduct disorder?

options.text: Low empathy and ability to identify interpersonal issues

correct_answer.text: Low empathy and ability to identify interpersonal issues

correct_answers.text: Low empathy and ability to identify interpersonal issues

questions.explanation: Both boys and girls with conduct disorder demonstrate low empathy and difficulty identifying interpersonal issues.

questions.question_text: Which of the following curves is a plot of (sensitivity) versus (1 – specificity) on either axis?
questions.explanation: A receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curve plots sensitivity against 1 – specificity as the cut-off criterion is varied.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding screening test dimensions?

options.text: For a screening test, the cut-off is set towards high sensitivity.
If prevalence <10% or >90%, the positive and negative predictive values are not representative.
Sensitivity is defined as the proportion of those people who have the disease who are currently detected by the test.
Specificity is defined as the proportion of those people who do not have the disease who are correctly left undetected by the test.
The more sensitive the test, the higher the positive predictive value.

correct_answer.text: The more sensitive the test, the higher the positive predictive value.

correct_answers.text: The more sensitive the test, the higher the positive predictive value.

questions.explanation: The more sensitive a test, the higher its negative predictive value; higher specificity raises the positive predictive value.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a measure of external validity of a randomized control test?
questions.explanation: External validity refers to the extent to which study findings can be generalized beyond the sample and setting.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of the normal distribution curve?

options.text: 10% of the values lie beyond two standard deviations (SDs) from the median.
68% of the values fall within one SD of the mean.
The mean, median and mode are equal.
The total area under the curve represents 100% of all values.
The spread from the mean is represented by the SD.

correct_answer.text: 10% of the values lie beyond two standard deviations (SDs) from the median.

correct_answers.text: 10% of the values lie beyond two standard deviations (SDs) from the median.

questions.explanation: In a normal distribution, about 5% of values lie beyond two standard deviations from the mean, not 10%.

questions.question_text: Based on Table 9.1, which of the following findings is incorrect?

options.text: Higher levels of noradrenaline are found in patients suffering from chronic asthma, and this finding is statistically significant at the 0.1% level.
Patients with acute asthma have the lowest neuropeptide Y (NPY) levels among three groups.
The differences in number of stressful life events encountered by patients with acute asthma, chronic asthma and healthy controls are not statistically significant.
There are statistically significant differences in ACTH in patients with acute asthma, chronic asthma and healthy controls, and this finding is statistically significant at the 5% level.

There are statistically significant differences in adrenaline between patients with acute asthma, chronic asthma and healthy controls, and this finding is statistically significant at the 0.01% level.

correct_answer.text: Higher levels of noradrenaline are found in patients suffering from chronic asthma, and this finding is statistically significant at the 0.1% level.

correct_answers.text: Higher levels of noradrenaline are found in patients suffering from chronic asthma, and this finding is statistically significant at the 0.1% level.

questions.explanation: Higher noradrenaline levels are found in acute asthma patients, not chronic asthma, and are significant at 0.1%.

questions.question_text: Based on Table 9.2, which of the following statistical tests was used to examine the independent associations?
questions.explanation: Multivariate linear regression was used to examine associations between a continuous dependent variable (IL-4) and multiple continuous independent variables.

questions.question_text: Referring to the footnotes under Table 9.2, what is the reason to control for variables such as age?

options.text: Age is a confounding factor, which may influence the IL-4 levels.
Age is an independent variable, which may influence the IL-4 levels.
Age is responsible for reverse causality, which may influence the IL-4 levels.
Age will cause a type I error, which may influence the IL-4 levels.
Age will cause a type II error, which may influence the IL-4 levels.

correct_answer.text: Age is a confounding factor, which may influence the IL-4 levels.

correct_answers.text: Age is a confounding factor, which may influence the IL-4 levels.

questions.explanation: Age is a confounding factor correlated with both perceived stress/NPY and IL-4 levels.

questions.question_text: Table 9.2 demonstrates important findings. Based on this table, which of the following findings is correct?

options.text: The NPY levels among patients with asthma was not a significant predictor of the IL-4 levels measured at baseline and 1 year later, after controlling for potential confounders.
Perceived stress among patients with asthma was a significant predictor of the IL-4 levels measured at baseline only but not 1 year later, after controlling for potential confounders.
Perceived stress among patients with asthma was a significant predictor of the IL-4 levels measured at baseline and 1 year later, after controlling for potential confounders.
Perceived stress among patients with asthma was a significant predictor of the IL-4 levels measured at 1 year later but not baseline after controlling for potential confounders.
Perceived stress among patients with asthma was not a significant predictor of the IL-4 levels measured at baseline and 1 year later, controlling for potential confounders.

correct_answer.text: Perceived stress among patients with asthma was a significant predictor of the IL-4 levels measured at baseline and 1 year later, after controlling for potential confounders.

correct_answers.text: Perceived stress among patients with asthma was a significant predictor of the IL-4 levels measured at baseline and 1 year later, after controlling for potential confounders.

questions.explanation: Perceived stress predicted IL-4 levels at both baseline and 1 year later after adjusting for confounders.

questions.question_text: Referring to the footnotes under Table 9.2, Sobel test was performed in model 3. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Age is a mediating factor in the association between high perceived stress levels and IL-4 overexpression in patients with asthma.
Asthma severity is a mediating factor in the association between high perceived stress levels and IL-4 overexpression in patients with asthma.
IL-4 is a mediating factor in the association between high perceived stress and NPY levels in patients with asthma.
NPY level is a mediating factor in the association between high perceived stress levels and IL-4 overexpression in patients with asthma.
Perceived stress is a mediating factor in the association between high NPY levels and IL-4 overexpression in patients with asthma.

correct_answer.text: NPY level is a mediating factor in the association between high perceived stress levels and IL-4 overexpression in patients with asthma.

correct_answers.text: NPY level is a mediating factor in the association between high perceived stress levels and IL-4 overexpression in patients with asthma.

questions.explanation: The Sobel test showed NPY level mediates the association between perceived stress and IL-4 overexpression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is related to outcome in autistic patients?
questions.explanation: The presence or absence of speech by age 5, along with patient IQ and severity of autism, consistently relate to long-term outcome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following instruments that assess autism in children does not require training?
questions.explanation: The PDDBI is a parent- and teacher-rated measure that does not require formal training.

questions.question_text: One common medical comorbidity of autism is epilepsy. Which of the following statements about epilepsy in autistic children is false?

options.text: Approximately 5% of children with autism have epilepsy.
Females have greater risk of seizure than males.
The risk of epilepsy is highest in early childhood.
The most common type of seizure is grand mal seizure.
The use of anticonvulsants may help to reduce self-injurious behaviour.

correct_answer.text: The most common type of seizure is grand mal seizure.

correct_answers.text: The most common type of seizure is grand mal seizure.

questions.explanation: Partial seizures are the most common type in autistic children, not grand mal seizures.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old man with repeated thefts of hair gel and OCD. Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding his condition?

options.text: Checking is the most common compulsion.
Fear of contamination is the most common obsession.
Obsessional image is a relatively uncommon obsession.
A PET scan may show hypermetabolism in the left orbital gyrus and both caudate nuclei.
Shoplifting is more common in OCD than in the general population.

correct_answer.text: Shoplifting is more common in OCD than in the general population.

correct_answers.text: Shoplifting is more common in OCD than in the general population.

questions.explanation: Shoplifting is not more common in OCD than in the general population.

questions.question_text: Which of the following substances can induce panic in an individual and provides evidence that panic disorder has a biological basis?
questions.explanation: Inhalation of sodium lactate provokes panic attacks, supporting a biological basis for panic disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding social phobia is false?

options.text: Alcohol abuse is not as common in social phobia as in other phobias.
Beta-blockers can be used to reduce autonomic arousal.
Taijin-kyofu-sho in Japan is a transcultural variant.
The first episode occurs in a public place, usually without any reason.
First-degree relatives of social phobics are three times more likely to be affected.

correct_answer.text: Alcohol abuse is not as common in social phobia as in other phobias.

correct_answers.text: Alcohol abuse is not as common in social phobia as in other phobias.

questions.explanation: Alcohol abuse is actually more common in social phobia than in other phobias.

questions.question_text: A 50-year-old man on multiple medications presents with anxiety. Which one of the following medications may be responsible?
questions.explanation: Systemic corticosteroids such as prednisolone are known to induce anxiety symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Fahr disease is false?

options.text: It is a rare autosomal-dominant disorder.
Patients present with cognitive impairment in the absence of mood or psychotic symptoms.
There is extensive calcification of the basal ganglia.
There is apathy and memory impairment but sparing of language function.

correct_answer.text: Patients present with cognitive impairment in the absence of mood or psychotic symptoms.

correct_answers.text: Patients present with cognitive impairment in the absence of mood or psychotic symptoms.

questions.explanation: Fahr disease often presents with mood or psychotic symptoms in addition to cognitive impairment.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old woman with anorexia nervosa using laxatives and diuretics. Which abnormality would you expect to find?
questions.explanation: Self-induced vomiting, laxative use and diuretics lead to hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an outcome that was assessed in the multimodal treatment study?
questions.explanation: Progression to conduct disorder was not one of the primary outcome measures in the multimodal ADHD treatment study.

questions.question_text: The combination of APOE e4 allele and traumatic head injury increases the risk for Alzheimer’s disease by how many times?
questions.explanation: APOE ε4 combined with traumatic brain injury multiplies Alzheimer’s disease risk by eight.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about adult sex offenders is false?

options.text: A majority begins their offending behaviour in middle age.
About 35% of sex offenders have a mental illness.
Lack of victim empathy predicts high risk of reoffending.
There is often a history of affectionless upbringing by unloving parents.
Treatment includes behavioural techniques on self-monitoring.

correct_answer.text: A majority begins their offending behaviour in middle age.

correct_answers.text: A majority begins their offending behaviour in middle age.

questions.explanation: Most adult sex offenders begin offending in adolescence, not middle age.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about the Psychopathy Checklist–Revised version (PCL-R) is false?

options.text: It is a 20-item rating scale, with each item rating from 0 (does not apply) to 2 (definitely applies).
It assesses interpersonal relationships of the individual.
It is a risk assessment tool.
It is able to differentiate psychopathy from antisocial PD.
Scores are based on both semi-structured and collateral information.

correct_answer.text: It is a risk assessment tool.

correct_answers.text: It is a risk assessment tool.

questions.explanation: The PCL-R identifies psychopathic traits but is not designed as a risk assessment tool.

questions.question_text: A 14-year-old girl with PTSD from sexual assault. Which of the following antidepressants would be most effective for her treatment?
questions.explanation: Sertraline has the strongest evidence for efficacy in pediatric PTSD and is FDA-approved for youth.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding reading disorder is incorrect?

options.text: The prevalence of dyslexia in the United Kingdom is 5%.
The prevalence of genuine dyslexia and mild dyslexia is 10%.
In the United States, 17%–20% of elementary school children are estimated to suffer from reading disabilities.
In the United States, 17%–20% of the US population displays a reading disability.
A survey across Japan, Taiwan and the US found reading disability rates of 8%, 8% and 7% respectively.

correct_answer.text: In the United States, 17%–20% of elementary school children are estimated to suffer from reading disabilities.

correct_answers.text: In the United States, 17%–20% of elementary school children are estimated to suffer from reading disabilities.

questions.explanation: The 17%–20% figure refers to the proportion of the total population with reading disabilities, not to elementary school children.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding childhood disintegrative syndrome is true?

options.text: It is associated with a high prevalence of epilepsy.
Most patients suffer from mild mental retardation.
The age of onset is before 2 years old.

correct_answer.text: It is associated with a high prevalence of epilepsy.

correct_answers.text: It is associated with a high prevalence of epilepsy.

questions.explanation: Childhood disintegrative disorder is rare but is associated with epilepsy in about 77% of cases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following MRI findings is not reported in children with schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Studies report increased superior temporal gyrus volume, not a decrease, in childhood-onset schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Children with major depression may present with atypical features. Which of the following is not a feature of childhood atypical depression?
questions.explanation: Atypical depression features weight gain rather than weight loss in children.

questions.question_text: What percentage of children with major depressive episodes may show signs of bipolar disorder by adolescence?
questions.explanation: About one-third (approximately 33%) of children with major depression may convert to bipolar disorder by adolescence.

questions.question_text: Childhood mania is often misdiagnosed. Which one of the following does not usually present in children with mania?
questions.explanation: Children with mania more often display irritability rather than classic euphoria.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a common feature of depression in adolescents?
questions.explanation: Adolescents with depression are less likely to show prominent psychomotor retardation than adults.

questions.question_text: Adjustment disorders are predictive of more serious mental disorders in which group of patients?
questions.explanation: In children and adolescents, adjustment disorders often predict more serious psychiatric illness later.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old man with neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Which one of the following is the most appropriate pharmacological treatment?
questions.explanation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is treated with dopaminergic agonists such as bromocriptine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the immune system of depressed patients is false?

options.text: There is a decrease in the ratio of T-helper to T-suppressor cells in peripheral blood.
There is an increase in the numbers of neutrophil in peripheral blood.
There is an increase in the level of IL-1 in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
There is an increase in the level of IL-6 in CSF.
There is an increase in the levels of acute-phase proteins in peripheral blood.

correct_answer.text: There is an increase in the level of IL-6 in CSF.

correct_answers.text: There is an increase in the level of IL-6 in CSF.

questions.explanation: CSF IL-6 levels are typically decreased in depressed patients, not increased.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old student with lifelong insomnia and late sleep onset. Which one of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Sleep disorder related to chaotic life in studying

questions.explanation: Delayed sleep-phase syndrome is characterized by delayed nocturnal sleep onset and difficulty waking in the morning.

questions.question_text: What percentage of the hospitalized elderly fulfil the criteria for a major depressive episode?
questions.explanation: Up to 21% of hospitalized elderly patients meet criteria for a major depressive episode.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a common comorbid psychiatric disorder in children and adolescents with MDD?
questions.explanation: Eating disorders are not a common comorbidity in pediatric major depressive disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the use of clozapine is false?

options.text: The combined use of clozapine and carbamazepine is a safe practice to prevent seizures.
The combined use of clozapine and lithium may help to reduce neutropenia.
Hyoscine may be used to treat hypersalivation in clozapine users.
The risk of agranulocytosis is independent of clozapine dose.
The risk of seizures increases with clozapine dose.

correct_answer.text: The combined use of clozapine and carbamazepine is a safe practice to prevent seizures.

correct_answers.text: The combined use of clozapine and carbamazepine is a safe practice to prevent seizures.

questions.question_text: You plan to start carbamazepine in a 35-year-old Asian woman. Which test do you perform first?
questions.explanation: Testing for HLA-B*1502 is essential in Asian patients to reduce risk of Stevens–Johnson syndrome with carbamazepine.

questions.question_text: In the use of electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) to treat schizophrenia, which particular aspect is most useful?
questions.explanation: ECT is especially effective for catatonic symptoms in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Baseline WBC count must be greater than which of the following before starting clozapine?
questions.explanation: Clozapine requires a baseline WBC ≥ 3,500/mm³ (ANC ≥ 2,000/mm³) to start therapy.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following comorbidities has been reported to occur most frequently in children diagnosed with ADHD?
questions.explanation: Speech or language impairments occur in about 50% of children with ADHD, more than other listed comorbidities.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Gilles de la Tourette syndrome is false?

options.text: ADHD is the most frequently occurring comorbidity.
Coprolalia does not appear until about 6 years after onset of motor tics.
Habit reversal training may reduce tics.
It affects more males than females.
Obsessions and compulsions in Tourette syndrome are similar to those of pure OCD without Tourette.

correct_answer.text: Obsessions and compulsions in Tourette syndrome are similar to those of pure OCD without Tourette.

correct_answers.text: Obsessions and compulsions in Tourette syndrome are similar to those of pure OCD without Tourette.

questions.explanation: Obsessions/compulsions in Tourette syndrome tend to differ in content from those in pure OCD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding separation anxiety is true?

options.text: It begins at around 15 months and peaks at 3 years.
It is not a normative part of development.
It is usually persistent and excessive.
The child’s experiences of previous separations vary with the rate of disappearance of separation anxiety.

correct_answer.text: The child’s experiences of previous separations vary with the rate of disappearance of separation anxiety.

correct_answers.text: The child’s experiences of previous separations vary with the rate of disappearance of separation anxiety.

questions.explanation: The intensity and duration of separation anxiety vary based on the child’s prior separation experiences and handling.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding bipolar disorder in the elderly is false?

options.text: Genetic factor is an important aetiology.
Increased cerebral vulnerabilities and insults play a more important role than life events in precipitating late-onset mania.
Neurological abnormalities are more common, especially in elderly male patients.
The prognosis is the same as that for bipolar disorder in younger people.
More rapid recurrences tend to be more common.

correct_answer.text: Genetic factor is an important aetiology.

correct_answers.text: Genetic factor is an important aetiology.

questions.explanation: Late-onset bipolar disorder shows less genetic loading than younger-onset cases.

questions.question_text: What percentage of people undergoing bereavement meet criteria for major depressive disorder?
questions.explanation: About 20% of bereaved individuals meet criteria for major depressive disorder.

questions.question_text: How long can cocaine metabolites remain detectable in urine?
questions.explanation: Cocaine metabolites can be detected in urine for up to 96 hours after use.
